gnoc-01-c1.text: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (2023). Coining a Word and Championing a Cause: The Story of Raphael Lemkin. Holocaust Encyclopedia, USHMM.
gnoc-01-c1.quote: While in Nuremberg, Lemkin also learned of the death of 49 members of his family, including his parents
gnoc-01-c1.claim: In 1944 Raphael Lemkin (1900–1959), a Polish-Jewish jurist who lost forty-nine relatives in the Holocaust, coined the word genocide in his book Axis Rule in Occupied Europe.

gnoc-01-c2.text: Avalon Project, Lillian Goldman Law Library, Yale Law School (1948). Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide; December 9, 1948. The Avalon Project, Yale Law School.
gnoc-01-c2.quote: genocide means any of the following acts committed with intent to destroy, in whole or in part,
gnoc-01-c2.claim: Article II defines genocide as acts "committed with intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnical, racial or religious group, as such."

gnoc-01-c2.text: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (2023). First conviction for genocide. Holocaust Encyclopedia, USHMM.
gnoc-01-c2.quote: issues the world's first conviction, in an international tribunal, for genocide.
gnoc-01-c2.claim: The first conviction by an international tribunal, Jean-Paul Akayesu at the ICTR, came only in 1998, fifty years after adoption.
